haiku-low.q1: At 10,000 rows or fewer, the click response is the CSV itself. Above 10,000, a row is recorded, a background job is queued, and the user gets 202 at once, then an email link.
haiku-low.q2: The click returns the existing active export with already_running true, plus its filters and columns. No second export starts.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours from sending. The bucket lifecycle rule deletes old files, and no cleanup job is built. The 7-day rule is stated only in storage helper comments.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with 60 s and 300 s waits between them. After the last failure, the user gets a failure email and the page shows failed with a generic message.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. Export state is kept on the primary. Which database holds the reports table is not stated.
haiku-low.q6: State is stored in the report_exports table on the primary. The page fetches the latest export on load and polls its status until done or failed.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, fills one 16 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. It never holds the whole report.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible before completion, and the object key stays empty, so no partial file is downloadable. The next attempt starts from row zero and aborts the abandoned upload.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and columns are copied from the page URL into the report_exports row. The job payload holds only export_id, and the job reads filters and columns from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on user_id and report_id where state is queued or running. A losing concurrent insert reads the winning row and returns it with already_running true.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed and the row marked done with object_key before the email is sent. If done with email_sent_at empty, the job only resends the email. If email_sent_at is set, it does nothing.
haiku-low.q12: The small path builds the CSV in memory, so nothing is stored. A failure or the 503 row cap returns an error, and the user retries. No partial file is produced.

sonnet.q1: reports.row_count (unfiltered, from the replica) decides. 10,000 or fewer: the click response is the CSV itself (buffered, text/csv attachment), nothing stored. Above 10,000: a report_exports row is created, a background job is enqueued, 202 returned at once; the user later gets an email with a download link (and the page shows status/download).
sonnet.q2: The click returns the existing active export with already_running: true (no new export). If the existing one is stale (Step 11), it is marked failed and a new export is created instead.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours (signed_url with 86400 s). The stored file is deleted by the bucket's lifecycle rule, stated as 7 days (no cleanup job built); links_until is set to t0 + 7 days, and the page link is min(24h, links_until - now). How the storage service enforces it is not known.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts total (waits of 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3). After the last failure, on_final_failure marks the row failed with a generic message, aborts the upload, and sends a report_export_failed email; the page shows failed with the message and a Try again button. (If the row is already done, it is left unchanged and no failure email is sent.)
sonnet.q5: The read replica, for report rows (small path, large job, and the row_count read). Export state is kept on the primary. Which database holds the reports table is not stated (Open Question 6).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database. The page fetches GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load (so it works when reopened later) and polls it: every 5 s, then every 30 s after the first 2 minutes, stopping on done or failed.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows from the replica in keyset pages of 5,000, builds CSV in one 16 MB in-memory buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part (about 57 parts, keeping only etags), so the whole report is never in memory. Completes the multipart upload at the end.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible at the object key because the multipart upload is not completed, so no partial file can be downloaded. The abandoned upload is aborted by the next attempt's Step 6 (best effort; the bucket's 24-hour rule discards leftovers). No progress is saved: the next attempt starts again from row zero, with a new attempt token and new upload.
sonnet.q9: They are validated and copied into the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row. The job payload carries only the export_id; the job loads the row to read filters and columns.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where state is queued or running on report_exports. The losing insert hits the index, then reads the winning row and returns it with already_running: true.
sonnet.q11: The row must first be marked done (fenced update, after complete_multipart succeeded); then the email is sent and email_sent_at is set. If the job runs again: row done with email_sent_at set, or missing/failed, it returns doing nothing; row done with email_sent_at empty, it does not re-export and only resends the email (raising to retry if that fails).
sonnet.q12: The request returns an error (read past the 60 s limit, read failure, or more than 10,000 rows read gives 503). The CSV is buffered, not streamed, so no truncated file is sent. No file, row or job is left; the user retries.
